result:
Done.

**Root cause:** `makeMove`'s `mkHalf:` block compared the moving piece against `WN` (knight, 2) instead of `WP` (pawn, 1), so knight moves reset the fifty-move clock and pawn moves incremented it — `movegen.inc:908`.

**Files touched**
- `variants/bug02/movegen.inc` — `cp WN` → `cp WP` (+ one comment line). The entire behavioural fix; assembles to exactly one changed code byte (tap offset 4434, `0x02→0x01`) plus the tape checksum, so no code-layout shift.
- `variants/bug02/test_fifty_move.py` — new, 23-case regression test (~13 s).
- `variants/bug02/Makefile` — new `test-fifty` target, run at the end of `make test`; added to `.PHONY`.
- `FIX_NOTES.md`, `STATE.md` — new, at workspace root.

**Gates**
- Reported symptom: PASS — hm 98 + `a2a3` → 0 (play); + `e8e7` → 1 (play); hm 40 + `Na1b3` → 41; hm 99 + quiet rook move still gives `Draw (50-move)`.
- `make test` (variant): PASS 6/6.
- New test: PASS 23/23 on the fixed tape; 12 ok / 11 failed on the pre-fix tape, so it demonstrably catches this bug. A failing run aborts make (verified end-to-end).
- Characterisation suite: PASS 57/57, exit 0 — up from 40 ok / 17 failed. Recorded from the pristine build, so this says the fix restores pristine behaviour exactly at every recorded point. (Needs `--harness ../harness`; its built-in default path points outside this workspace.)
- Review: one synchronous round, **category-A findings: none** → gate closed at round 1 of 3.

**Knowingly left open** (all recorded in `FIX_NOTES.md`; none in the reported scope)
- Reviewer category-B findings B1/B3/B6/B7 were fixed anyway. Chasing B1 exposed a real defect in my own test helper — `run_takeback` typed all moves at one frame, which the game cannot see — now fixed; the take-back case was vacuous and is not any more.
- Not fixed: the engine-move path isn't pinned by the new test (it is pinned by four characterisation cases, and scripting engine moves is the documented flakiness risk here); the clock wraps at 255 with no saturation (unreachable through the UI, pre-existing, byte-identical before and after); a position loaded with a clock already ≥100 doesn't declare the draw until the next move (pre-existing, matches pristine); no genuine 100-half-move game (the emulator's 5:00 clock flag-falls past ~35 plies); the test requires the harness.
